content:
Instagram now has a new iPhone-exclusive feature that can automatically create Reels videos. Users simply need to select video clips and tap once to generate a edited work.

However, Meta is very cautious about implying that this feature can replace creators' manual editing skills, so as not to cause their dissatisfaction...

This cautious approach even extends to the naming of the feature: the new feature is called First Draft, meaning it only provides a starting point for creation.

The company has shared operational procedures and result demonstrations on Threads.

Users can also choose to create a first draft edit immediately after filming.

There are two ways to use this feature: 1. Open the Reels media library → select one or more clips → tap the 'First draft' button at the bottom of the screen → review the edit → enter the full editor or publish directly. 2. Open the camera in Instagram → film content → tap the 'First draft' button → review the edit → enter the full editor and then publish.

Some creators questioned why this feature is placed in the main Instagram app rather than Edits. The company responded that if users need it, this feature can be provided in both apps. Currently this feature is only available on the iPhone version, and the Android version is expected to be launched later.
